title: Nifty holds 25,000 after volatile session; PSU Banks surge 3.7%, IT drags - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Markets closed marginally higher on Monday after a choppy session, as investors chose selective buying over broad profit-taking following last week’s near 8.5 per cent rally.

The Sensex ended at 81,106.65, up 107.25 points or 0.13 per cent, while the Nifty settled at 25,044.65, gaining 58.25 points or 0.23 per cent, after swinging between a high of 81,339.41 and a low of 80,519.31 on the Sensex through the day.

“After the sharp rally, some consolidation would be healthy for the market,” said Ajit Mishra, SVP, Research at Religare Broking, noting that foreign investors have pumped over $4.1 billion into Indian equities so far in November, providing a floor to any dip.

PSU Banks led all gainers, surging 3.7 per cent, while Pharma and Healthcare also ended higher. IT was the day’s biggest drag, falling over 1.2 per cent, as global concerns around AI-related capital expenditure continued to weigh on the sector. Metals slipped 0.5 per cent and Telecom also ended lower.

Bank Nifty outperformed, closing above 59,700, breaking out of a four-month range between 54,000 and 58,500, with analysts now eyeing 60,500–61,000 as the next target.

Broader markets saw limited movement. The Nifty Midcap 100 gained 0.55 per cent and the Smallcap 100 edged up 0.1 per cent, reflecting some caution after the recent run-up.

On the BSE, 1,757 stocks advanced against 2,517 declines. Data from Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund showed that in October, the Nifty 50 was the only major index to post positive returns at 1.91 per cent, while Microcap and Smallcap indices fell 8.95 per cent and 5.81 per cent respectively, underlining how concentrated the recent recovery has been in large caps.

HSBC upgraded India to overweight from neutral in its Asia equity strategy, citing resilient earnings, more reasonable valuations and strong credit growth, while downgrading China to neutral.

“We see strong credit growth, resilient earnings and measures supporting growth and the currency,” wrote Herald van der Linde, Head of Equity Strategy at HSBC Asia Pacific, adding that India “offers diversification and low volatility in Asian markets dominated by AI stocks.”

On the currency front, the rupee snapped a five-day winning streak, retreating slightly after state-run banks bought dollars ahead of Tuesday’s market holiday.

The USD/INR traded around 93.70, with Dilip Parmar of HDFC Securities noting key support at 93.50 and resistance at 94.30, as markets await US October CPI data for the next directional cue.

In commodities, WTI crude traded around $91 per barrel, well below last month’s peak of $135. COMEX gold gained about 1.3 per cent to around $4,130, while silver rose 2.2 per cent to around $53.10.

MCX gold gained about 1 per cent to ₹143,970 and MCX silver advanced 1.9 per cent to around ₹188,600, with the rupee’s strength limiting domestic gains relative to international prices.

With markets shut on Tuesday, Wednesday’s session will take its cue from US October CPI data due Tuesday and India’s own inflation print on Thursday. Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments, flagged that “crude oil prices and global risk sentiment remain key near-term monitorables,” while Siddhartha Khemka of Motilal Oswal pointed to hopes around US-Iran diplomacy and slower AI capex as factors that could continue to support large-cap Indian equities in the sessions ahead.
